artifacts.summary: Confirms --depends-on-add is unreachable for not_started tasks (map_status() has no arm resolving to not_started); recommends shape (a) -- a new no-op-only operation:target_status arm, edge-only-guarded -- over shape (b) (standalone operation) on call-site-count grounds; finds the 421->497 edge from acceptance criterion 5 is now moot because task 497 has completed and archived out of active_projects.

memory_candidates.content: update-task-status.sh's --depends-on-add flag is restricted to calls whose operation:target_status pair resolves to the task's own CURRENT status (a no-op replay), reusing that vehicle rather than inventing a second one for 'just add an edge'. map_status()'s closed case statement has no arm that resolves to not_started, so the flag is structurally unreachable for any not_started task -- the single most common status needing edge backfill. orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh's resolve_noop_token()/propose_edge_for_pair() independently anticipate this exact gap today, falling back to a propose-only notice whenever the higher task in a collision pair is not_started.

--depends-on-add's missing-predecessor refusal checks active_projects[].project_number only -- a predecessor that has completed and been archived out of active_projects (into specs/archive/state.json) is treated as nonexistent, even though it genuinely existed and finished. An edge-backfill task description written against a task's then-current contending/live predecessor should be re-verified against live state.json at implement time, since a predecessor can complete and archive between research and implement dispatches, making the edge both infeasible (refused) and moot (the ordering risk it would have prevented is already resolved by fact).
